module_title: Economic Survey - Basic Facts & Macroeconomic Indicators
introduction: The Economic Survey is presented by the Ministry of Finance just before the Union Budget. It serves as the report card of the country's economy for the previous financial year. According to the latest survey, despite global uncertainties, the Indian economy remains resilient and continues to be the fastest-growing major economy in the world.

core_concepts.title: GDP Growth Rate
core_concepts.description: The real GDP growth rate for the current financial year is estimated at 7.4%. For the upcoming financial year, the growth projection is pegged between 6.8% and 7.2%.

core_concepts.title: Inflation (CPI)
core_concepts.description: Average retail inflation (CPI) fell to a historic low of 1.7% during the April-December period. This was primarily driven by a decline in the prices of food items like vegetables, pulses, and spices.

core_concepts.title: Fiscal Deficit
core_concepts.description: The government has maintained fiscal discipline. The fiscal deficit target has been reduced from 4.8% (Provisional Actuals) to 4.4% (Budget Estimates) for the upcoming financial year.

core_concepts.title: Forex Reserves
core_concepts.description: India's foreign exchange reserves have surged to $701.4 billion, which is sufficient to cover 11 months of imports and 94% of the total external debt.

core_concepts.title: Private Consumption Growth
core_concepts.description: Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) has increased to 61.5% of the GDP, marking its highest level since 2011-12. This indicates strong domestic demand in the economy.

important_entities.name: Nirmala Sitharaman
important_entities.significance: Presents the Economic Survey document in the Parliament.

important_entities.name: Chief Economic Advisor (CEA)
important_entities.significance: The Economic Survey is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs under the guidance of the CEA.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Current Year vs. Upcoming Year Growth
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Read the question carefully. The estimated growth for the 'current' year is 7.4%, while the 'projection' for the 'upcoming' year is 6.8%-7.2%. Do not confuse the two.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A simple way to remember: Both the Fiscal Deficit target (4.4%) and the estimated GDP growth (7.4%) end with '.4'.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct data-based questions (e.g., 'What is the current Forex Reserve?' - $701.4 Billion) are highly frequent in SSC and State PSC exams.
Pay special attention to the CPI inflation rate (1.7%) as it is unusually low and likely to be asked.
